project.name: harness-kit
project.description: Project-agnostic AI agent harness with stage orchestration, bounded loops, and MCP context tools.

docWorkflow._note: Set mode=doc-workflow to activate. All verifier thresholds are overridable via CLI flags to doc-verifier.mjs.

toolSubset._note: When mode=doc-workflow, only these non-code tools are active. Extend as needed.

verifier._note: Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease: 90+=Very Easy, 80+=Easy, 70+=Fairly Easy, 60+=Standard, 50+=Fairly Difficult, 30+=Difficult. Score 60 targets general-public readability.

wordCountThresholds._note: Set min/max for whole-document, and per-section overrides under 'sections'.

noAiSlop._note: Warning-first rollout for deterministic low-signal phrase checks. Set mode=error to hard-fail.

modeMappings._note: Machine-readable skill, loop, and model assignments per harness mode. Used by the proxy, HTTP adapter, and Open WebUI integrations.

assistant.description: Quick-answer, one-shot. No architecture stage. Fastest response.

dev.description: Code delivery with light review. Skips architect and review-depth.

full.description: All 7 harness stages, cross-model review, maximum quality.

hardwareProfiles._note: Hardware-specific tuning. Set HARNESS_HW_PROFILE=<key> to activate a profile's env defaults. The harness does not auto-detect hardware; operators copy the env block into their shell profile or systemd unit.

proxmox-lxc-xeon-v3-50gb.description: Dell R630, 2× Xeon E5-2640 v3 (Haswell, 8c/socket, 16 physical cores), 50 GB RAM, SSD, no GPU. Ollama in Proxmox LXC container. AVX2, no AVX-512.

lxcConfig._note: Paste these into /etc/pve/lxc/<CTID>.conf on the Proxmox host, then restart the CT.
lxcConfig.cores_minimum_note: 16 cores (both sockets, all physical) is the real minimum — 8 cores (single socket) causes the model to appear unresponsive on 7b+ models due to insufficient parallelism.
lxcConfig.memory_mb_note: 50 GB assigned to the container — matches the full server RAM.
lxcConfig.cpuset_note: Socket 0 physical cores + their HT siblings. Prevents cross-socket NUMA latency.
lxcConfig.cpuset_both_sockets_note: All 16 physical cores across both sockets — required for usable inference. Use this if NUMA pinning causes model stalls.

recommendedGenerationModels.note: Best coder quality; ~10 t/s with 16 physical cores
Fastest; ~18 t/s; best for loops and assistant
Highest quality; ~4 t/s; leaves ~28 GB headroom

_notes: LXC is near-native for CPU workloads — do NOT use a KVM VM for Ollama (AVX2 passthrough adds complexity for no benefit).
SSD: model cold-start is ~10-15s for 14b (vs ~25s on HDD). Subsequent prompts are unaffected.
NUMA: v3 dual-socket has 2 NUMA nodes (8 cores + ~25 GB each). Pin to node 0 to avoid cross-socket latency.
HT: OLLAMA_NUM_THREADS=16 uses physical cores only; hyperthreads hurt llama.cpp throughput.
LXC memory: set container memory limit >= model_size_gb + 4 GB overhead. For 14b: limit >= 13 GB.
LXC cpuset: optionally pin to socket 0 with 'lxc.cgroup2.cpuset.cpus: 0-7,16-23' in the CT config.

harnessEnv._MODEL_ID_NOTE: Copy the exact model identifier from LM Studio → My Models → hover model → Copy Identifier. The paths above are examples; your installed identifiers may differ.

commands._note: These commands are used by convergence loops (build-fix, test-fix) and the validation matrix. Replace them with your project's actual commands. The harness-kit repository itself does not define lint/build/test — adopting projects must override these values. Commands can be a string (e.g. 'npm run lint') or a parameterized object with a vars schema (see test-filter example below).

modelPolicy.description: Phase 5 five-tier capability model (GA: 2026-07-25, hosted Copilot refresh: 2026-09-23). Canonical per-skill routing is in skillModelMapping — consult that section for the primary model and fallback chain of any specific skill. Copilot Auto remains a safe general default; skillModelMapping overrides it for the 20 harness skills. See .github/harness/phase5/validation-results/model-routing-benchmark-refresh-2026-09-23.md for the current hosted Copilot evidence.

tiers.ultra-reasoning: Novel problem-solving, multi-stage conflict adjudication, and frontier architecture decisions. Skills: architect, feedback. Primary models: gpt-6-astra, claude-opus-5-5, gpt-6-sol. 2026-09 hosted Copilot refresh: Astra leads long-horizon quality signals; GPT-6 Sol is the lower-cost powerful fallback.
tiers.high-reasoning: Sustained multi-hop reasoning over large contexts. 13 skills covering Understand, Review Breadth, Review Depth, Teach, and most analysis skills. Primary models: claude-opus-5-5, gpt-6-sol, claude-opus-5. 2026-09 hosted Copilot refresh: Opus 5.5 improves review/knowledge value; GPT-6 Sol covers OpenAI-only policy lanes.
tiers.balanced-coding: Fast, accurate code generation with reasoning balance. Skills: prototype, implement, run-loop. Primary models: gpt-5.6-terra, claude-sonnet-5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.3-codex. 2026-09 hosted Copilot refresh: Terra is the balanced everyday interactive and agentic coding lane.
tiers.fast-execution: Speed-optimised, cost-aware execution. Skill: budget-aware-execution. Primary models: gpt-6-luna, gemini-3.8-flash, mai-code-1.1-flash. Phase 5b quality baseline: 0.748.
tiers.universal-fallback: Claude Haiku 4.5. Guaranteed availability for all 20 skills as last-resort cascade terminator. Quality: ~0.68 (acceptable for failover).

modelPolicy.crossModelReview: For an active route containing implement, its effective implementation model must differ from every active review-stage model. The router enforces this after resolving role defaults, stageModels, and selected stageModelSets; configuration cannot disable the guardrail. If both are on Copilot Auto, explicitly select distinct models for the review-fix pass to break single-model echo chambers.
modelPolicy.autoNote: Copilot Auto is a safe default when no skill-specific override applies. For the 20 harness skills, prefer the primary model from skillModelMapping for best Phase 5 performance.

domainSpecialists.description: Advisory model-tier guidance for domain-heavy work inside the existing stage machine. This metadata is not consumed by prompt-router; executable stage routing remains owned by skillModelMapping.mappings.

frontend.useFor: React/component implementation, stateful UI behavior, accessibility fixes, and frontend test repair after an Architecture Brief is settled.
frontend.reviewPairing: Use high-reasoning review for design-system, accessibility, routing, or cross-page changes.

ui-ux.useFor: Interaction design, information architecture, design critique, complex user-flow tradeoffs, and product-quality review.
ui-ux.reviewPairing: Pair with a balanced-coding implementer for final UI code so design judgment and code generation stay distinct.

database.useFor: Schema design, migrations, query correctness, data integrity, concurrency, and rollback planning.
database.reviewPairing: Require high-reasoning review and explicit validation for destructive migrations or production data paths.

infrastructure.useFor: IaC, CI/CD, deployment topology, environment configuration, permissions, and rollout or rollback plans.
infrastructure.reviewPairing: Keep approvals explicit for secrets, destructive commands, permission expansion, or production deployment changes.

backend.useFor: Service implementation, API behavior, shared types, orchestration code, tests, and targeted refactors.
backend.reviewPairing: Use high-reasoning review for auth, caching, tenancy, distributed systems, or cross-module contracts.

localDecisionSidecar.description: Optional typed-decision advisor. FROZEN — see the freeze block below before changing enabled or mode.

freeze.reason: Technically feasible and measured (67-71 ms, 2.0 GB, 10/12 with 0 confident-wrong), but no open decision model meets the durability bar. Every wire-compatible candidate comes from a single author, the family is days old, and v3 silently broke the v1/v2 readout contract.
freeze.retainedBecause: The lite backend, eval instrument, fixture, and word-boundary router fix are independently valuable and already merged. Freezing is a sourcing decision, not a quality one.
unfreezeRequires: A wire-compatible open decision model published by an organisation rather than a single individual, OR the existing family sustained and unbroken for at least two further releases.
A pinned model revision with a documented, versioned readout contract that cannot change silently under the same identifier.
At least 100 human-labelled or history-derived cases in .github/harness/eval/decision-intent-cases.json.
Zero confident-wrong on that human-labelled set.
A fresh Architecture Brief and human approval; this Brief authorises freezing only.

hardwareFit.notes: Ryzen 7 7800X3D, 64 GB RAM, RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB. Requires local CUDA latency, memory, calibration, and jevcompat evidence before any authority change.

measuredCandidates.outcome: All five probe tasks returned uncertain against this repository's intent profiles. Calibrated low confidence is the correct behavior for an unfamiliar label set; it is not evidence of usable accuracy.
Produced confidently wrong selections (p up to 0.9996) on probes a calibrated scorer marked uncertain. Not suitable as a decision scorer.

skillModelMapping.description: Phase 5c GitHub Copilot model assignments (validated 2026-07-25 via multi-model optimizer; hosted Copilot refresh 2026-09-23). 5-tier strategy: Ultra-Reasoning (2 skills), High-Reasoning (13 skills), Balanced-Coding (3 skills), Fast-Execution (1 skill). September 2026 hosted refresh promotes GPT-6 Astra/Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Terra, GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and MAI-Code-1.1-Flash where supported by GitHub Copilot. Universal fallback: Claude Haiku 4.5. See .github/harness/phase5/validation-results/model-routing-benchmark-refresh-2026-09-23.md for current hosted evidence.

high-reasoning.use_for: Multi-hop reasoning, architectural judgment, cross-cutting analysis

pr.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: Multi-model optimizer identified Opus 5 as +3% better for PR creation (+25bp quality gain). Deeper multi-PR reasoning across complex decision logic. Phase 4 baseline (+252.3%) maintained. Fallback: GPT-5.5 for eval-first patterns, Opus 4.8 as safety net.

eval-first-tuning.reasoning: Phase 5 shift: GPT-5.5 specialized for eval-driven workflows with high keyword distinctiveness. Better than Phase 4's Opus 4.8 for procedural evaluation patterns. Alternative: Opus 4.8 for baseline evaluation.

remember.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: Opus 5 demonstrates +3% quality gain for knowledge synthesis from architecture briefs. Enhanced reasoning depth for pattern extraction from 200K context. Fallback: Opus 4.8 for baseline synthesis, Sonnet 5 for speed.

feedback.reasoning: 2026 benchmark refresh: GitHub model comparison and LiveBench place GPT-5.6 Sol in the deep-reasoning lane, while Luna is optimized for cheap/fast tasks. Sol becomes primary for conflict adjudication; Opus 5 and GPT-5.5 remain high-reasoning fallbacks.

prototype.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: Multi-model optimizer identified GPT-5.4 +5% quality gain for throwaway prototypes. Better reasoning balance for prototype validation vs. Sonnet 5's pure code generation. Maintains Phase 4 +219% improvement with superior reasoning. Fallback: Sonnet 5 for speed.

architect.reasoning: 2026 benchmark refresh: GPT-5.6 Sol is the GPT-5.6 deep-reasoning model for complex reasoning over large codebases and long-running agentic work. Luna is retained for cheap/fast packages, not architecture primaries.

understand-process.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: Opus 5 demonstrates +3% quality for graph-first impact analysis. Enhanced reasoning depth for multi-layer dependency tracing. 200K context handles complex change graphs. Fallback: GPT-5.5 for procedural analysis, Opus 4.8 as baseline.

doubt-driven-development.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: Opus 5 demonstrates +6.4% quality for security skepticism + correctness validation. Enhanced multi-stage rigor for high-stakes changes. Fallback: GPT-5.5 for procedural security checks, Opus 4.8 as baseline analysis.

setup-harness-bootstrap.reasoning: Phase 5c MAJOR UPGRADE: GPT-5.5 demonstrates +9% quality (HIGHEST UPSIDE in optimizer run). Superior at methodical step-by-step procedural guidance for bootstrap workflows. Fallback: Opus 4.8 for deep procedural analysis, Gemini 3.6 for speed.

implement.reasoning: Phase 5 shift: GPT-5.4 provides superior reasoning + code balance vs. Codex's pure specialization. Better for architectural implementation guidance with Phase 4 baseline (+130%). Fallback: Codex if pure code generation needed.

review-breadth.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: Opus 5 demonstrates +3% quality for wide-pass review. Superior multi-dimensional reasoning across correctness, standards, safety, completeness. Fallback: GPT-5.5 for procedural review, Opus 4.8 as baseline.

budget-aware-execution.reasoning: Phase 5 shift: Cost-awareness + token tracking task benefits from speed optimization. Gemini 3.5 Flash is production-grade for fast, cost-aware analysis (cf. 'budget' in skill name). Maintains Phase 4 improvement while prioritizing speed.

deterministic-validation.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: Opus 5 demonstrates +6.4% quality for proof selection and objective exit criteria. Enhanced logical rigor and deterministic reasoning for validation patterns. Fallback: GPT-5.5 for procedural validation, Opus 4.8 as baseline.

context-engineering.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: GPT-5.5 demonstrates +5.4% quality for session memory hygiene and task-switch checkpointing. Superior at state management and checkpoint logic. Fallback: Opus 4.8 for stable multi-turn reasoning, Sonnet 5 for speed.

retrieval-quality-ops.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: GPT-5.5 demonstrates +5.4% quality for A/B evaluation orchestration. Superior comparative reasoning for retrieval stack analysis. Fallback: Opus 4.8 for stable evaluation baseline, Gemini 3.6 for speed.

observability-and-instrumentation.reasoning: Telemetry patterns, RED metrics, and structured logging require methodical guidance. Opus 4.8 strong for procedural documentation and instrumentation best practices.

ai-techniques-radar.reasoning: Phase 5c upgrade: Opus 5 demonstrates +2.8% quality for AI techniques evaluation. Enhanced frontier model awareness for cutting-edge techniques. Fallback: GPT-5.5 for latest trends, Opus 4.8 for established techniques.

teach-agent.reasoning: Knowledge synthesis and educational content creation require deep, clear reasoning. Opus 4.8 proven for teaching-oriented guidance patterns.

run-loop.reasoning: Phase 5 shift: Loop orchestration requires code clarity + execution logic balance. Claude Sonnet 5 balances both for clear loop structures vs. Opus 4.8's general reasoning. Maintains Phase 4 improvement (+99.5%) with better code orientation.

review-depth.reasoning: Structural review (ownership, boundaries, reuse, Brief conformance) requires consistent deep analysis. Opus 4.8 excels at structural consistency. Note: Phase 4 lowest performer (+83.2%) but still strong improvement. Opus 5 for ultra-complex structures.

commandDispatch.description: MCP command dispatch configuration for cross-project command execution. Adopting projects can customize timeout and audit path.

auth.description: Role-based command authorization is enforced before command execution. Configure rolePermissions explicitly; unknown roles and commands are denied.

oauthHardening.description: Slice E OAuth hardening semantics. Use HARNESS_OAUTH_ISSUER or set issuer for canonical issuer binding checks. Empty issuer defaults to HARNESS_HTTP_URL at runtime.

governance.description: Paths checked by scripts/harness/protected-path-guard.mjs (npm run harness:protected-paths:check). Warn-only by default; set HARNESS_ENABLE_PROTECTED_PATH_GATE=true or pass --strict to block. Override this list per-project without touching the script.

compaction.description: T3 (anthropic-context-compaction.md): scripts/harness/context-compaction.mjs. run-experiment.mjs keeps the most recent maxRecentIterations one-line history entries verbatim and compacts older ones into a single summary line; plan-review.mjs keeps full critique text for the most recent maxRecentRounds and compacts older rounds to verdict-only lines.

scratchNotes.description: T5 (anthropic-agentic-memory-file-notes.md): opt-in per-run scratch notes file for run-experiment.mjs (--scratch-notes or HARNESS_EXPERIMENT_SCRATCH_NOTES=true). Off by default; kept separate from committed harness memory.

contextGrowth.description: Warn-only prompt-size tripwire (scripts/harness/run-experiment.mjs, scripts/harness/plan-review.mjs). Composed-prompt character count is a rough proxy (~4 chars/token), not a measured token count, since these loops shell out to an arbitrary agent CLI with no token-usage channel. Crossing the threshold only warns and records promptChars; it never blocks a run. See .github/harness/memory/radar/anthropic-context-compaction.md.
